# AAPL — research (cumulative)

## Business and moat

Source: FY2025 Form 10-K (period ended 2025-09-27), read from the local extracts item-1.txt and notes.txt [S100]. Quotes are verbatim from the sections named.

- 2026-10-14 · **Intangible assets (brand, IP) — supported, qualitative.** Item 1, Competition lists "corporate reputation" among its competitive factors [S100]. Item 1, Intellectual Property: the company "holds a broad collection of intellectual property rights" [S100]. The same section limits the claim: "No single intellectual property right is solely responsible for protecting the Company’s products" [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Switching costs / ecosystem — supported only indirectly.** Item 1, Competition cites "a strong third-party software and accessories ecosystem" [S100]; Services text says content is kept available "across multiple Apple devices" [S100]. The filing does not state switching costs or quantify lock-in; this is an inference, not a filing claim.
- 2026-10-14 · **Network effect — no evidence.** Item 1 does not claim one, and states "The Company has a minority market share" [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Cost advantage — no evidence.** Item 1 says competitors "seek to compete primarily through aggressive pricing and very low cost structures" [S100]; it also notes the company "uses some custom components that are not commonly used by its competitors" [S100], which is a differentiation statement, not a cost claim.
- 2026-10-14 · **Efficient scale — no evidence.**
- 2026-10-14 · **Distribution mix (context).** Item 1, Markets and Distribution: direct and indirect channels were "40% and 60%" of net sales [S100].

## Management

- 2026-10-14 · **Capital-allocation priorities (Item 7, Capital Return Program).** In May 2025 the company announced a new repurchase program of up to $100 billion and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26 per share [S100]; in fiscal 2025 it repurchased $89.3 billion of common stock and paid $15.4 billion in dividends and equivalents [S100]. The program "does not obligate the Company to acquire a minimum amount of shares" [S100]. The company "intends to increase its dividend on an annual basis" [S100]. A prior $110 billion program (announced 2024-05-02) had its final $19.8 billion used in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 (Item 5) [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Net-cash-neutral statement — no evidence.** The phrase "net cash" appears nowhere in the full 10-K text; the filing states no net-cash-neutral target [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Dividend since the 10-K.** Board declared $0.27 per share on 2026-07-30, payable 2026-08-13 [S103].
- 2026-10-14 · **Acquisitions and divestitures, last three fiscal years — no evidence.** Item 7 names none and notes one through thirteen contain no business-combination note; the only mention is Item 1A: "has invested, and in the future may invest, in new business strategies, commercial relationships and acquisitions" [S101].
- 2026-10-14 · **CEO succession.** Apple announced on 2026-04-20 that John Ternus (SVP Hardware Engineering) becomes CEO on 2026-09-01 and Tim Cook becomes executive chairman; Arthur Levinson moves from non-executive chairman to lead independent director [S108]. A secondary report confirms the change took effect and that Ternus joined the board [S109]. The press release says the board approved the change unanimously after long-term succession planning [S108].
- 2026-10-14 · **Executive statements, Q3 FY2026 call.** Cook called it Apple's strongest June quarter ever, per the press-release summary [S103]; the CFO said the quarter set June-quarter records for EPS and operating cash flow [S103]. Cook characterised the memory-price surge as a once-in-a-century flood, per press coverage [S105]. These are management's own views, paraphrased from summaries.

## Risk evidence

- 2026-10-14 · **Item 9A material weakness — answered, none reported.** Management concluded its internal control over financial reporting "was effective as of September 27, 2025" [S100]; the phrase "material weakness" does not appear in Item 9A, and no change in internal control in the fourth quarter affected it materially [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Auditor's report, going concern — absent.** Ernst & Young LLP states "the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects" the financial position [S100]; it reports an unqualified opinion on internal control, and the words "going concern" and "substantial doubt" appear nowhere in the report or the filing [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Customer concentration, net sales — no evidence.** Note thirteen (segment information) and the rest of the filing name no customer by share of net sales and make no statement that none exceeded the threshold; Item 1 gives only the channel split, "accounted for 40% and 60%, respectively" for direct and indirect channels [S100].
- 2026-10-14 · **Customer concentration, receivables (Note 4).** "one customer that represented 10% or more of total trade receivables" at 12%; third-party cellular network carriers were 34% of trade receivables (38% a year earlier) [S102]. Two vendors each held 10% or more of vendor non-trade receivables, at 46% and 23% [S102]. This is receivables, not revenue concentration.
- 2026-10-14 · **Named risk factors bearing on a 5–10-year thesis (Item 1A, ≤5)** [S101]:
  1. Trade and geopolitics: "The Company’s business can be impacted by political events, trade and other international disputes…" [S101].
  2. Supply concentration: "depends on component and product manufacturing and logistical services provided by outsourcing partners" [S101].
  3. Legal: "currently subject to antitrust investigations and litigation" [S101].
  4. Competition: "Global markets for the Company’s products and services are highly competitive" [S101].
  5. Ecosystem: future performance "depends in part on support from third-party software developers" [S101].
